text.p: Pacific Research & Engineering Thursday announced financial results for the first quarter ended March 31, 1997.

Revenue for the first quarter was $2,291,204, up 17.5 percent over revenue of $1,950,367 in the same quarter last year. For the quarter, the company posted a net loss after taxes of $13,779, or 1 cent per share, compared with net income of $190,169 in the year-ago quarter, due primarily to expenses related to new product development and marketing.

"We are greatly encouraged by our strong revenue performance during the quarter and by the upturn in our markets' purchasing activity," stated Jack Williams, president and chief executive officer of PR&E.

"Many of the ownership groups which made station acquisitions soon after the ratification of the Telecommunications Reform Act last February returned to the marketplace for products and services to support the broadcasting efforts of their newly formed station groups.
"Additionally, cost of sales remained relatively stable, with only a slight increase from the year-ago quarter," said Williams. "As a result, our gross profit margin for the
quarter was stronger, at 43.5 percent, than the 41.6 percent we reported last year at this time."

Williams said the quarter's net loss was largely attributable to the significant investment made in the marketing of three new products which were recently introduced at trade shows in the United States and Europe. He also pointed out that the company had never before developed and introduced more than one product in any three-month period of its history.
